question: During Chandragupta Maurya’s reign, the administration of Pataliputra, which was the capital of the Mauryas was managed by how many committees?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Six**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During Chandragupta Maurya's reign, the administration of Pataliputra, the capital of the Mauryas, was managed by six committees.
 
• These committees were responsible for different aspects of the city's administration and functioning.
 
• Each committee had its specific domain such as industry, foreigners, birth and death registration, trade, etc.
 
• This administrative setup ensured a structured and efficient management of the capital city.
 
• The information about these committees is derived from the accounts of Megasthenes, a Greek ambassador to the Maurya court.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta Maurya**

 
 
• He was the founder of the Maurya Empire in ancient India.
 
• He reigned from 322 BCE to 298 BCE.
 
• Chandragupta was a pivotal figure in unifying most of the Indian subcontinent under one empire.
 
 
 
• **Megasthenes**
 
 
• He was a Greek ambassador who visited India during Chandragupta Maurya's reign.
 
• His accounts provide valuable insights into the Mauryan administration and society.
 
• His work 'Indica' is one of the primary sources of information about ancient India during that period.
 
 
 
• **Maurya Empire**
 
 
• It was one of the largest empires in the Indian subcontinent, founded by Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• The empire saw significant expansion under his rule and that of his successors, particularly Ashoka the Great.
 
• The Maurya Empire played a crucial role in spreading Buddhism both within and beyond India.
